body:
STOPPED before claim. This issue defines separate sub-issues for the catalog cases.

Upstream main e5b0ca3c11bcea6803cd11afe906bb5665be0545 already contains the catalog infrastructure from commit 854a3af014aeadb9b23bfa3c6696d3f3b79d301b (Fixes #2393).
The catalog contains one case: examples/catalog/2d/first-part.
The remaining operation families and documentation links are absent.
This issue is only partly implemented.

Expected-refusal cases also need catalog support.
The current checks require a successful script and an NC file.
The Wire Contour test deliberately refuses posting in crates/app/tests/mcp_wire_contour.rs.
Caught host errors still make scripts fail in crates/app/src/script/mod.rs.
The operation registry has no separate laser kind.

Recommendation: use the per-case sub-issues specified in this issue.
Keep effort:high for bounded case work.
Do not close this umbrella after one case.
No claim, branch, source change, build, or test was made.

## Research result for #2392

Source: `upstream/main` at `5fdbed9bd`. I used only our code and our issues. I wrote no code.

The issue has no list of questions. I took these eight questions from its text and from the earlier comment.

### Answers

**1. What does the catalog have now?**
The infrastructure of #2393 is on main. One case exists: `examples/catalog/2d/first-part` (Face, 2D Pocket, Drill).
- Layout and rules: `examples/catalog/README.md`.
- Build tool: `xtask/src/catalog.rs` (`cargo xtask catalog [--case] [--check] [--screenshots] [--pdf]`).
- Test: `crates/app/tests/example_catalog.rs`. It finds each case folder automatically. A new case needs no new test code.

**2. Can a script build each family?**
Yes for the document steps. `cam.call(tool, args)` in `crates/app/src/script/call.rs` runs each MCP tool on the command history of the script. The tools `add_setup`, `load_machine`, `set_setup_post`, `set_wcs`, `import_dxf`, `add_fixture` and `add_operation` exist in `crates/app/src/mcp/`. `add_operation` resolves the kind from the registry (`crates/app/src/mcp/edit.rs:229`).
I did not run a script for each kind. A case can find a missing parameter in a tool. That is a new `area:mcp` issue, not a part of the case.

**3. Which operation kinds exist?**
`KindInfo::ALL` in `crates/app/src/operation/kinds.rs` has 45 kinds:
- 2D: Face, 2D Contour, 2D Pocket, Slot, Trochoidal slot, Trace, 2D Adaptive, 2D Offset, Engrave, 2D Chamfer, Circular, Thread, Drill, Bore, Deburr.
- 3D: 3D Pocket, 3D Finish.
- Multi-axis: 5-Axis Contour, 5-Axis Parallel, Swarf, Advanced Swarf, Rotary Contour, Rotary Parallel, Rotary Offset, Multi-Axis Rough, 5-Axis Flow, Multi-Axis Contour.
- Turning: Facing, Profile Rough, Profile Finish, Groove Rough, Groove Finish, Parting, Threading, Chamfering, Taper Turning, Multi-Pass Turning, Form Turning, Boring.
- Other: Probe, Plasma Profile, Wire Contour, Sinker Burn, Sinker Side Burn.

There is no laser kind. A search for "laser" in `crates/app/src/operation`, `crates/app/src/schema.rs` and `site/content/guide/operations` finds nothing. A laser case is not possible until a laser kind exists. That is a design decision for the maintainer, not catalog work.

**4. Can a case show a refusal?**
Not today. Three places prevent it:
- `every_catalog_case_opens_regenerates_verifies_and_posts_byte_for_byte` asserts `OpStatus::Ok`, no blocking warning, an empty verification report and a successful post.
- `every_catalog_case_rebuilds_from_camscript` asserts exit 0 and a written `.nc`.
- The script host records each refusal in the `errors` list of the run, also when the script catches it (`crates/app/src/script/mod.rs`, `dispatch`). Thus a script with a caught refusal does not end clean.

The third point is a deliberate law ("a job that swallowed its refusals is not a clean job"). The catalog must not weaken it. The proposal below keeps it.

**5. Are screenshots and PDFs done?**
The commands exist (`xtask/src/catalog_media.rs`, `xtask/src/catalog_pdf.rs`). The output is not published.
- The default branch name is `catalog-screenshots`. Upstream does not have that branch. Upstream has `screenshots`, and the files that I listed there are issue and PR images.
- `collect_pngs` takes one PNG for each case (`catalog/<family>/<case>/<case>.png`). The guide images in `docs/images/` show one image for each operation (`first-part-1-face1.png`). The catalog does not do this.
- `--screenshots` needs a GPU or a software adapter. It cannot be a gate step.

**6. Do the docs link the cases?**
No. The operation pages are `site/content/guide/operations/operations-{2d,3d,turning,edm,plasma,probing}.md` and `site/content/guide/multi-axis/operations-multiaxis.md`. Each kind has its own `##` heading. The files in `site/content/guide/operations/` do not contain "catalog" or a link into `examples/`.

**7. How does this relate to #2394 and #2582?**
- #2394 (cone with a threaded end) is the first case and is open. Its blocker (#2393 not merged) is gone. It can start now.
- #2582 (QA swarm) proposes that each QA part that posts becomes a catalog case. It is `P8` and `needs-maintainer`. The proposal here does not depend on it. The case layout already fits it.

**8. Does the test scale to many cases?**
Not well. The two tests are single loops over all cases. The first failure hides the other cases, and the time of all cases adds up in one `#[test]`. AGENTS.md "Testing" moves a test of more than about 60 s in debug to the heavy lane. I did not measure the time. The 3D and multi-axis cases are the risk.

### Design proposal

Smallest useful slice first.

**Slice 1 - cases that need no new infrastructure.** Work #2394. Add one case for each of the 2D kinds that the seed case does not show. These use only what is on main. Each case is one folder and no Rust code.

**Slice 2 - docs links.** A generated "Example cases" list under each kind heading of the operation pages. `cargo xtask catalog --check` fails if a case names a kind that has no link, or a link names a case that does not exist. A new file `case.toml` in each case folder holds the data: `kinds = [...]`, `machine`, `expect`. The README stays prose.

**Slice 3 - expected refusals.** `case.toml` gets `expect = "post"` (default) or `expect = "refusal"`. A refusal case has no `.nc`. It has `refusal.txt` with the exact refusal lines. The script does not catch the refusal. The script run ends with an error, and the test compares the `errors` list with `refusal.txt` byte for byte. The host law of question 4 stays as it is: the refusal is still recorded, and the catalog asserts it. The script saves the project before the refused step. Thus the first test can open it and assert the same refusal.

**Slice 4 - test scaling.** Split the two loops so that one failure names its case and the other cases still run. Give each case a time budget. A case over the budget goes to the heavy lane with its lane named in the ignore reason, or gets a smaller model.

**Slice 5 - media.** One image for each operation plus a blank, as `docs/images/first-part-*.png` does. Publish to one images branch. Decide the branch: reuse `screenshots` under `catalog/`, or create `catalog-screenshots`. I recommend `catalog-screenshots`, because `screenshots` holds review evidence under issue and PR numbers. The docs link the raw files of that branch. PDFs stay optional and local (`target/catalog-pdf/`).

**Slice 6 - the other families.** Turning, 3D, multi-axis, EDM, plasma, probing, in that order. One sub-issue for each case, filed when the case before it in the family is merged, as the issue text says.

Dropped options:
- A Rust test file for each case. Dropped: the discovery loop already covers a new folder, and a file for each case adds many files to `crates/app/tests/`.
- A `try/catch` in the script for refusal cases. Dropped: it works against the host law and hides which refusal occurred.
- Images in the product tree. Dropped: the issue and `xtask/src/catalog_media.rs` forbid it.

### Proposed sub-issues

I did not file these. This issue is `P4` and does not have `needs-research`. My instructions file sub-issues only for a `needs-research` issue. #2394 already exists and is not in the list.

Priority rule used: `P4` where the words of the maintainer in this issue name the work ("a bunch of examples", "testing the various operations", screenshots on a separate images branch, docs off the operation pages). `P6` for the rest. The maintainer can change each one.

"Case done" in the table means: the case folder obeys `examples/catalog/README.md`, the catalog tests pass, and the README says what to look at.

| # | Title | What it does | Done means | P | Effort | Area |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | Catalog: `case.toml` and the example links on the operation pages | Adds `case.toml` (kinds, machine, expect) to each case and generates the "Example cases" list under each kind heading. | `cargo xtask catalog --check` fails on a case without a link and on a link without a case. The seed case shows under Face, 2D Pocket and Drill. | P4 | medium | area:build |
| B | Catalog: a case can expect a refusal | Adds `expect = "refusal"` with `refusal.txt`. The two catalog tests compare the recorded refusal lines with the file. | One refusal case passes. A changed refusal text makes the test red. The script host law does not change. | P4 | high | area:build |
| C | Catalog: one test result for each case, with a time budget | Splits the two loops so that a failure names its case and the other cases still run. Moves a case over the budget to the heavy lane. | Two broken cases give two named failures. The `#[test]` count does not go down. No default-lane case takes more than about 60 s in debug. | P4 | medium | area:build |
| D | Catalog: an image for each operation, published to the images branch | Renders a blank and one image for each operation of a case, and commits them to the images branch. The README and the docs link them. | The branch holds the images of each case at stable paths. No PNG is in the product tree. The seed case README shows its images. | P4 | medium | area:build |
| E | Example case: 2D contour with lead-in and tabs | A plate cut out with 2D Contour. | Case done. | P4 | medium | area:2d |
| F | Example case: 2D Adaptive roughing, then a 2D Pocket finish | Roughs an open pocket with 2D Adaptive and finishes the wall. | Case done. | P4 | medium | area:2d |
| G | Example case: slot and trochoidal slot | One part with a Slot and a Trochoidal slot of the same width. | Case done. | P4 | medium | area:2d |
| H | Example case: hole work - Drill pattern, Bore, Circular, Thread | A plate with a bolt circle, a bored hole and a milled thread. | Case done. The posted program shows the canned cycles and the helix. | P4 | medium | area:2d |
| I | Example case: edge work - 2D Chamfer, Deburr, Engrave, Trace | Chamfers and deburrs the edges of a plate and engraves a mark. | Case done. | P4 | medium | area:2d |
| J | Example case: turning - groove rough, groove finish and part-off | A bar with an outside groove, parted off. Uses `assets/machines/lathe.mch`. | Case done. The posted program shows the groove plunges and the part-off. | P4 | medium | area:turning |
| K | Example case: turning - Boring, Chamfering, Taper Turning, Multi-Pass Turning, Form Turning | A bushing that shows the turning kinds that #2394 and J do not show. Two cases if one is too long. | Case done. Each of the five kinds is in a case. | P6 | medium | area:turning |
| L | Example case: 3D Pocket roughing and 3D Finish (parallel and waterline) | A small domed part: 3D Pocket, then two 3D Finish patterns. | Case done. The case stays in its time budget, or is in the heavy lane. | P4 | medium | area:3d |
| M | Example case: 3D rest machining | A second, smaller tool clears what the first tool left. | Case done. The README shows the rest region. | P6 | medium | area:3d |
| N | Example case: 3+1 indexed and 3+2 tilted 2D work | A block with pockets on two indexed faces and one tilted face. | Case done. The posted program shows the index moves. | P6 | medium | area:multiaxis |
| O | Example case: wrapped A axis - Rotary Contour, Rotary Parallel, Rotary Offset | A cylinder with a wrapped groove. | Case done. | P6 | medium | area:multiaxis |
| P | Example case: 5-axis - Swarf, 5-Axis Contour, 5-Axis Flow | A tilted wall cut by Swarf and a surface cut by Flow. | Case done. The collision check is clean. | P6 | high | area:multiaxis |
| Q | Example case: Wire Contour, and a taper that the machine refuses | A wire-cut profile from a DXF, and a second case that expects the taper refusal. Needs B. | The post case passes. The refusal case compares its `refusal.txt`. | P6 | medium | area:post |
| R | Example case: Sinker Burn and Sinker Side Burn | An electrode burn on `assets/machines/sinker-edm.mch`. | Case done. | P6 | medium | area:post |
| S | Example case: Plasma Profile | A plate cut from a DXF on a plasma machine file. | Case done. The posted program shows the pierce and the lead-in. | P6 | medium | area:2d |
| T | Example case: Probe before a Face | A probing cycle, then a Face operation. | Case done. | P6 | medium | area:post |

Order: #2394, E to I and A can start now and do not depend on each other. B comes before Q. C comes before L. D can come at any time.

Notes for the maintainer:
- No laser case is proposed (question 3). A laser kind needs its own design issue first.
- The effort labels for cases are `effort:medium`, as on #2394. A case adds a recorded program and changes no generator. If you read the safety floor differently, the cases become `effort:high`.
- There are no `area:edm`, `area:plasma` or `area:probing` labels. I used the nearest existing label.
- Not checked: I did not run `add_operation` for each kind from a script. I did not check which machine file fits the wire and plasma cases, or which post each machine file selects. I ran no build and no test.

This umbrella stays open.

## Sub-issues filed for #2392

The research comment above (2026-11-20T05:00Z) has the answers and the design proposal. It said that this issue does not have `needs-research`. The issue has that label now. Thus I filed the 20 proposed sub-issues. I checked the proposal again against `upstream/main` at `5fdbed9bd`. It is still correct.

Two details changed from the proposal table:
- The Plasma Profile case names its machine file: `assets/machines/tormach-1300pl.mch` (kind `plasma`).
- The Wire Contour case names its machine file: `assets/machines/sodick-alc400g.mch`. Its description says that the post refuses each taper (#1800).

### Order

- #2394, #2855 and #2859 to #2863 can start now. They do not depend on each other.
- #2856 comes before the refusal case of #2871.
- #2857 comes before #2866.
- #2866 comes before #2867.
- #2858 can come at any time.

### For the maintainer

- The priorities are proposals. `P4` is on the work that your words in this issue name. The other cases are `P6`. Change each one as you see fit.
- Each sub-issue is in the enhancement lane. The lane has two slots, thus the 20 issues do not start together.
- No laser case is filed. The operation registry has no laser kind. A laser kind needs its own design issue.
- There are no `area:edm`, `area:plasma` or `area:probing` labels. I used the nearest existing label.
- Not checked: I did not run `add_operation` for each kind from a script. I ran no build and no test.

This umbrella stays open for your review.

The work on #2859 (case `2d/contour-tabs`, PR #2877) found one bug: #2876. `add_operation` refuses `lead: { arc: ... }` for a 2D Contour, because the merge patch keeps the seeded linear lead. The message does not name the cause.
Found while building #2862: #2898. Circular with several radial passes produces links that verification blocks. The example uses a smaller circular hole that verifies without warnings.
The work on the case `2d/slots` (#2861) found one bug: #2906. A Slot wider than the tool leaves up to 0.86 mm in its round ends, and `verify` is ok.

The A-axis case #2869 cannot show Rotary Contour with the current generator.
It refuses a cylindrical workpiece along X and directs the user to Rotary Parallel.
Issue #3000 tracks this refusal.
The guard and its existing test are listed there.

Found a post refusal while working on #2872.
The shipped sinker post refuses Sinker Side Burn and emits no burn code for it.
Bug #3001 tracks the required post support.
This prevents the sinker catalog case from showing both posted burns.

The plasma catalog case #2873 is blocked by existing issue #1870. Plasma Profile refuses DXF generation on upstream/main 58cb641ca. The diagnostic says that a toolpath from DXF profile chains is not generated yet. The reproduction and held branch are recorded on #2873.

Found #3004 while building #2868. Indexed pockets retain the world stock height as a local cap and report false shank collisions. The report names the source lines and the original dimensions. No safety check was removed.

The work on #2865 found four verification refusals on combined turning shapes.

- #3005: Boring reports 11.5425 mm rest when the bushing has other outside features.
- #3006: Chamfering reports 0.0944 mm rest on a tapered stepped bar.
- #3007: Taper Turning reports 38.9500 mm rest on a stepped bar.
- #3008: Multi-Pass Turning reports 2.2543 mm rest on a short neck window.

Each report gives the original meridians, operation parameters and a passing comparison.
The simpler probes keep tolerance 0.05 and 48 angular segments.
The catalog work keeps all verification checks active.
These reports are related to #2880, which concerns Profile Finish.
The exact shared cause is not yet proved.

#2871 found a refusal: a Wire Contour on a DXF profile does not generate (`a toolpath from the chains of a DXF profile is not generated yet`). #2022 already tracks it. #2871 is blocked until #2022 covers the Sodick wire post and #2856 merges.
claim by this account's agent released (stale: no open PR, branch commit or comment for 4 h) - issue is free again (automatic sweep, AGENTS.md 4 h rule)
